answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may post offers or vote. If a challenge reveals that several accounts share one controller, the protocol merges their influence and forfeits deposits, rather than treating each account as a new person. This makes a Sybil attack costly: the attacker must tie up real capital for every fake identity and risks losing it when caught. A gale of fabricated accounts may begin a voyage, but each still needs a deposit to leave the jetty.
